title: Last duty assignment: Army medical command in Japan
description: Larry's DD-214 lists his last duty assignment as a U.S. Army medical command at APO San Francisco 96343 under U.S. Army Japan (USARJ) — an APO that served Camp Zama, Japan. So he finished his service in Japan, not Vietnam. Whether this was a routine reassignment or connected to medical treatment is not yet known; the form's box for wounds received in action reads NONE. This assignment fits the cool-season Tokyo photographs and his memory of seeing the Stars and Stripes report of his own death while in Japan.
researchNotes: The unit line on the family's photo of the form is partly illegible ('...USA MED COMD APO SF 96343 USARJ'); a sharper scan or the NPRC personnel file should give the exact unit designation and the dates of the Japan assignment. Key follow-ups: ask Larry what took him to a medical command in Japan; check whether the Tokyo photo series (VN-0093, VN-0095, and the rest) dates from this assignment rather than an R&R trip.
